title: Scheduler refactor changed kernel routing heuristics leading to tail-latency uplift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A scheduler refactor deployed to runtime-1.19.0 unintentionally changed the kernel routing heuristic used by the runtime to pick attention kernels. Starting 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC we observed a 30-60% increase in p99 token latency for a subset of long-sequence chat workloads (seq_len 1024-2048) on the 80-series GPU fleet. Impact: affected hosted customers using large open models with fused-attn available; Dedicated clusters with pinned kernel profiles were not affected.

This ticket contains the incident follow-up, root-cause analysis, mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC - Alert: p99 latency spike detected on prod-nyc cluster for model: redwood/gptx-13b-open. Alerts triggered by SLO on per-route p99 token latency.
2025-02-14 03:20 UTC - On-call triage: initial mitigation - route traffic to standby model variant with explicit fused-attn kernel pinning; latency improved for affected customers.
2025-02-14 04:05 UTC - Rollback: rolled back scheduler refactor ab/opt heuristic in prod-nyc; baseline p99 returned to normal within 10 minutes.
2025-02-15 10:00 UTC - Postmortem kickoff; gathered traces, kernel selector logs, and KV cache metrics for affected requests.

2025-02-17 15:30 UTC - Root cause identified: refactor introduced a cost-model change that favored lower-memory-footprint kernels for small batch sizes; for certain sequence length distributions this preference chose a non-fused attention kernel which increases per-token latency at tail percentiles.

2025-02-20 09:45 UTC - Long-running mitigations approved: reintroduce explicit fused-attn preference when model + sequence length distribution suggests fused kernel benefits; add telemetry to measure kernel choice by (model, seq_len, batch_size).
root_cause: During scheduler refactor we changed the kernel routing score to prioritize estimated GPU memory footprint over steady-state per-token cycles, without adequate coverage for multi-modal sequence length workloads.

The kernel selector scoring omitted a fused-attention win condition when the estimated workspace allocation exceeded a heuristic threshold for small batches. This threshold was tuned for throughput-heavy workloads and regressed tail latency for interactive chat workloads.

Kernel telemetry was sparse for the affected model shape: the shape-mapper had never seen seq_len > 1024 for that model in the training set, so the new heuristic never learned the fused-attn advantage for that regime.
Automated integration tests for kernel selection did not include cross-product coverage of (model, seq_len, batch_size, dtype) after the refactor, so the change slipped through presubmit.
mitigation: Hotfix: rolled back the new heuristic in prod within 50 minutes of alerting (2025-02-14).
Traffic-level mitigation: route affected routes to model variants with kernel-profile pinned until heuristic is validated.
Telemetry add: instrument kernel-choice logging tagged by model, seq_len_bucket, batch_size, dtype and export to per-route traces/dashboard.
Canary policy: add staged rollout with kernel-choice microbenchmarks and synthetic workloads for each canary node.
Safety net: emergency fallback policy to force fused-attn kernel selection for known models/sequences if p95/p99 exceeds threshold.
action_items: ENG-20322: Add deterministic integration tests for kernel selector covering 5 representative sequence length buckets and batch sizes (owner: SRE-team) - estimate 5
ENG-20323: Add telemetry pipeline for kernel-choice metrics and dashboards by model/seq_len_bucket (owner: Observability) - estimate 3
ENG-20324: Restore explicit fused-attn preference rule and add config flag:kernel_routing_mode (owner: Runtime) - estimate 8
ENG-20325: Add presubmit check that runs kernel-selection microbenchmarks for PRs touching scheduling or kernel-selection logic (owner: CI) - estimate 3
ENG-20326: Create a canary workload suite that simulates long-sequence interactive chat traffic for runtime-staging (owner: QA) - estimate 5
ENG-20327: Postmortem write-up and customer comms draft for any customers who saw degraded tail latency (owner: Incident Lead) - estimate 2
comments: 2025-02-14 04:20 UTC - Miguel O.: Rolled back change and confirmed p99 back to baseline. Need better pre-merge coverage for kernel-selection; opening follow-up tickets.
2025-02-15 11:05 UTC - Aisha P.: Initial triage indicates scoring delta in kernel routing. Collecting detailed traces and kernel selection logs for the last 72h.
2025-02-16 09:30 UTC - Priya Shah: Observability team will add tag 'kernel_choice' to trace spans and expose a histogram by seq_len_bucket. ETA 72h.
2025-02-18 13:40 UTC - Dan Lee: Drafted PR to reintroduce fused-attn preference when fused kernel expected win; unit tests added for basic shapes. Pending perf benches.
2025-02-20 16:55 UTC - Miguel O.: Bench results: for seq_len 1536 fused-attn is ~40% lower p99 at small batch sizes. Merging revert+tests after review.
2025-02-21 10:02 UTC - Release Manager (Olivia B.): Scheduling patch to runtime-1.19.1 as a point release with backported test suite. Target rollout 2025-02-25.
2025-02-21 11:15 UTC - Incident Lead (Aisha P.): Postmortem draft uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INCIDENTS/2025-02-14-scheduler-kernel-routing
notes: Lessons learned: kernel selection heuristics must be validated against percentile-sensitive workloads; throughput-focused heuristics can unintentionally harm interactive tail latency.
We need an explicit taxonomy of workload shapes (interactive vs throughput) and a config surface to pin kernel routing behavior per workload class.
CI safeguards: require microbenchmark coverage for scheduler and kernel-selection changes and fail PRs that alter scoring without a documented benchmark matrix.
Follow-up: incorporate synthetic long-sequence replay into canary gates; ensure Dedicated customers can opt into aggressive kernel optimizations separately from hosted defaults.
Owner for follow-ups: Miguel Ortega (runtime) and Priya Shah (observability)
